source_text: Nunc igitur de inerrabili gloria Dei in providentia videas memorari; tamen, ut mens parva poterit, conabor ostendere. Ut Adam illum per septimanam reformaverit, atque universae suae creaturae subveniret, nativitate filii sui Jesu Christi Domini nostri factum est. Quis itaque lege Dei doctus, quis plenus Spiritu sancto, non respiciat corde, ea die Gabriel angelum Mariae virgini evangelizasse, qua die draco Evam seduxit; ea die Spiritum sanctum Mariam virginem inundasse, qua lucem fecit; ea die in carne esse conversum, qua terram et aquam fecit; ea die in lacte esse conversum, qua stellas fecit; ea die in sanguine, qua terra et aqua foetus suos ediderunt; ea die in carne esse conversum, qua die hominem de humo instruxit; ea die natum esse Christum, qua hominem finxit; eadem die esse passum, quo Adam cecidit; ea die resurrexit a mortuis, qua lucem fecit.
pass_a_gloss: Now therefore about unerring glory of-God in providence you-may-see to-be-recalled; yet, as mind small will-be-able, I-will-try to-show. That Adam that through week he-might-have-reformed, and to-entire his creation he-might-help, by-nativity of-son his Jesus Christ Lord of-us it-has-been-done. Who therefore by-law of-God taught, who full with-Spirit holy, would-not look-back with-heart, on-that day Gabriel angel to-Mary virgin to-have-evangelized, on-which day dragon Eve seduced; on-that day Spirit holy Mary virgin to-have-flooded, on-which light he-made; on-that day into flesh to-have-been-turned, on-which earth and water he-made; on-that day into milk to-have-been-turned, on-which stars he-made; on-that day into blood, on-which earth and water offspring their brought-forth; on-that day into flesh to-have-been-turned, on-which day human from soil he-built; on-that day to-have-been-born Christ, on-which human he-fashioned; on-same day to-have-suffered, on-which Adam fell; on-that day he-rose from dead, on-which light he-made.

lemmas.gloss: to have been turned into flesh
on the same day to have suffered

pass_b_english: So now you may see the unerring glory of God in providence being recalled; yet, as far as a small mind can, I will try to show it. That he might remake that Adam through the week, and bring help to his whole creation, was accomplished by the birth of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

Who, then, taught in God’s law, who filled with the Holy Spirit, would not see in the heart that on the day the dragon seduced Eve, the angel Gabriel brought good news to the Virgin Mary; that on the day he made light, the Holy Spirit flooded the Virgin Mary; that on the day he made earth and water, he was turned into flesh; that on the day he made the stars, he was turned to milk; that on the day earth and water brought forth their young, he was in blood; that on the day he built the human from soil, he was turned into flesh; that on the day he fashioned the human, Christ was born; that on the day Adam fell, he suffered; that on the day he made light, he rose from the dead.

choices.choice: printed Migne/Wikisource continuous lock for Christ–Adam day chain
choices.rejected: ANF-only English or Walker conjectures as base
choices.why: Latin print is the lock; OCR corroborates; sixth-day image locus already mined as victorinus_creation.

choices.choice: remake that Adam through the week
choices.rejected: recreate humanity in seven ages as free allegory
choices.why: Keep Latin Adam illum / per septimanam / reformaverit without expanding into unstated schemes.

choices.choice: turned into flesh / into milk / in blood
choices.rejected: ANF ‘incarnate’ / ‘put to the breast’ / ‘circumcised’ as lock wording
choices.why: Pass B stays close to in carne / in lacte / in sanguine; ANF glosses noted only as compare.

anf_compare.notes: Sense matches ANF day-typology paragraph; Pass B prefers Latin idiom over ANF ‘circumcised’ for in sanguine.
